successCriteria.description: `AuditService` class exists in `src/modules/audit/audit.service.ts` and implements `IAuditService` from `./audit.service.interface`
`AuditService` constructor accepts the shared `pool` (from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`) as its dependency
`AuditService.record()` inserts a row into the `audit_records` table and returns the created `AuditRecord` with `id` and `createdAt` populated
`src/shared/types/index.ts` barrel re-exports `AuditAction` (already defined in the file; ensure it is present in the export list)
All new and modified files pass `tsc --noEmit` (strict TypeScript, no implicit any, strict null checks)

constraints: AuditService must NOT import or depend on any module other than `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, `./audit.service.interface`, `./audit.model`, and `../../shared/types` — it is a foundational module with zero internal module dependencies per the reconciled architecture dependency map

The `record` method must generate a unique `id` (UUID) and set `createdAt` to the current timestamp server-side — the caller provides `Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>` and the implementation fills those two fields

The `record` method must use parameterized queries (e.g. `$1, $2, …`) — no string concatenation or template interpolation of values into SQL, per the no-hardcoded-secrets and SQL-injection-prevention constraints

The `audit_records` table insert must map the `AuditRecord` fields to snake_case column names consistent with the existing `EmployeeRepository` pattern (`entity_type`, `entity_id`, `performed_by`, `created_at`)
outOfScope: Unit tests for `AuditService` — these belong to sibling sub-phase "Sub-phase 3: Unit tests for employee and audit modules"
Employee module implementation files (`employee.repository.ts`, `employee.service.ts`, `employee/index.ts`) — these belong to sibling sub-phase "Sub-phase 1: Employee module implementation"
Database migration for the `audit_records` table — the table is assumed to exist; this phase only implements the service that writes to it

ambiguities.description: The PLAN says "Constructor takes the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`" (suggesting constructor injection), but the existing `EmployeeRepository` imports `pool` at module level as a side-effect import. Which pattern should `AuditService` follow?
options: Constructor injection: accept `pool` as a constructor parameter (testable, matches PLAN wording)
Module-level import: import { pool } directly (matches EmployeeRepository precedent, simpler)

entityInvariants.invariant: Every `AuditRecord` returned by `record()` must have a non-empty `id` (UUID), a non-empty `createdAt` (Date), and all caller-supplied fields (`entityType`, `entityId`, `action`, `performedBy`, `changes`) preserved exactly as passed
`AuditRecord.action` must be one of the `AuditAction` enum values — the type system enforces this at compile time; the implementation must not widen or coerce the action field

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at this layer — the AuditService is a low-level infrastructure service; RBAC is enforced by the callers (controllers/services) that invoke `record`
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must reject with a typed error if the database insert fails (e.g. connection error, constraint violation); must not silently swallow errors

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `AuditService` constructor signature must match the pattern established by `EmployeeRepository`: accept the shared `pool` import from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` as a constructor parameter (not import it internally as a module-level side-effect)
The `record` method signature must exactly match `IAuditService.record`: accept `Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>` and return `Promise<AuditRecord>`
The `AuditRecord` type used in the service implementation must be the one from `./audit.model` — no local redefinition or structural divergence
The `src/modules/audit/index.ts` barrel export must follow the same re-export pattern as `src/modules/employee/index.ts`: named re-exports of the model, interface, and implementation

integrationPoints.why: AuditService uses the shared PostgreSQL pool for inserting audit records
